description: Critical smoke tests for the loci-preflight plan-mode GATE — the single behavior that matters most: does the skill invoke when (and only when) the user is in /plan mode? Per SKILL.md, preflight is 'MANDATORY in /plan mode' and must 'NOT invoke ... outside plan mode'. The suite is five tests in two controlled groups: (1) three /plan prompts that MUST invoke, (2) two no-/plan prompts whose wording SOUNDS like planning ('how should I modify', 'walk me through the plan') but, lacking the /plan prefix, MUST stay silent. Tests are paired by task so the ONLY difference between an invoke and a no-invoke case is the /plan signal: pf-critical-1 <-> pf-critical-5 (bounds guard on Connection_getConnIndex) and pf-critical-2 <-> pf-critical-4 (TX byte counter in HCI_SendDataPkt). All functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out, so a real /plan run produces a full report (not a STOPPED block). Two further evals ride in this file rather than gating invocation: pf-loops-1 (loop-cost reasoning) and pf-recipe-1 (what Step 1 does when the installed CLI is older than a flag `loci analyse prepare` needs). Both are reasoning-graded and run no tools.
note: Set $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT to your local BLE project root before running. NOTE: run_evals.sh keeps a leading '/plan' verbatim (it strips other slash commands) — that prefix is the plan-mode signal these tests gate on. Bash grading detects invocation via the '## Preflight:' header plus an 'Execution fit:' verdict line, matching the current SKILL.md output format.

evals.prompt: /plan Implement a bounds guard at the top of Connection_getConnIndex in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble_profiles/app/app_connection.c that returns -1 immediately if the connection handle is greater than or equal to MAX_NUM_BLE_CONNS, so callers never index past the connection table. The function is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: User is in /plan mode and describes new logic, so preflight is MANDATORY. A preflight report appears in the response text (before any plan body): a '## Preflight: Connection_getConnIndex' header, a conclusion table, and a bolded 'Execution fit: GOOD|ADJUST PLAN|STOP' verdict.

assertions.text: Response includes a '## Preflight:' section header
assertions.description: /plan mode + 'Implement a bounds guard' (new logic) must invoke the skill

assertions.text: Response includes an 'Execution fit:' line with value GOOD, ADJUST PLAN, or STOP
assertions.description: A proper invocation produces the verdict line per the SKILL.md output format

evals.prompt: /plan How should I modify HCI_SendDataPkt in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/simplelink-lowpower-f3-sdk/source/ti/ble5stack_flash/hci/cc26xx/hci.c to add a static uint32_t per-connection TX byte counter that accumulates the dataLen parameter on each successful send and wraps silently? The function is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: User is in /plan mode and the wording 'How should I modify' is an explicit SKILL.md trigger, so preflight is MANDATORY. A '## Preflight: HCI_SendDataPkt' report with an 'Execution fit:' verdict appears in the response before the modification plan. (This is the positive twin of pf-critical-4, which is the same task WITHOUT /plan.)

assertions.text: Response includes a '## Preflight:' section header
assertions.description: /plan mode + 'How should I modify' must invoke the skill

assertions.text: Response includes an 'Execution fit:' line with value GOOD, ADJUST PLAN, or STOP
assertions.description: A proper invocation produces the verdict line per the SKILL.md output format

evals.prompt: /plan Add a bond check inside HCI_SendDataPkt in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/simplelink-lowpower-f3-sdk/source/ti/ble5stack_flash/hci/cc26xx/hci.c that calls GAPBondMgr_FindAddr to reject packets from unbonded peers before the packet is sent. The HCI data path must complete within 10us at 48 MHz. Both functions are compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: User is in /plan mode and describes adding a new callee on a timing-constrained hot path, so preflight is MANDATORY. A '## Preflight: HCI_SendDataPkt' report appears with an 'Execution fit:' verdict — likely ADJUST PLAN or STOP given the NV-reading GAPBondMgr_FindAddr against a sub-10us budget, but any GOOD/ADJUST PLAN/STOP verdict satisfies the invocation gate.

assertions.text: Response includes a '## Preflight:' section header
assertions.description: /plan mode + 'Add a bond check' that introduces a new callee must invoke the skill

assertions.text: Response includes an 'Execution fit:' line with value GOOD, ADJUST PLAN, or STOP
assertions.description: A proper invocation produces the verdict line per the SKILL.md output format

evals.prompt: How should I modify HCI_SendDataPkt in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/simplelink-lowpower-f3-sdk/source/ti/ble5stack_flash/hci/cc26xx/hci.c to add a static uint32_t per-connection TX byte counter that accumulates the dataLen parameter on each successful send and wraps silently? The function is compiled into $LOCI_TEST_BLE_FRESH/basic_ble.out.
evals.expected_output: Identical task to pf-critical-2 but with NO /plan prefix — the user is NOT in plan mode. The phrase 'How should I modify' is a SKILL.md trigger word, but SKILL.md gates triggers on plan mode ('Do NOT invoke ... outside plan mode'). The skill must stay silent: a direct answer with NO '## Preflight:' header and NO 'Execution fit:' verdict.

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain a '## Preflight:' header
assertions.description: No /plan prefix — plan-sounding trigger wording must NOT invoke the skill outside plan mode

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain an 'Execution fit:' verdict line
assertions.description: No preflight report should be emitted when the user is not in plan mode

evals.prompt: How should I approach adding a bounds guard at the top of Connection_getConnIndex in $LOCI_TEST_BLE_ROOT/examples/rtos/LP_EM_CC2340R5/ble5stack/basic_ble_profiles/app/app_connection.c so it returns -1 when the connection handle is greater than or equal to MAX_NUM_BLE_CONNS?
evals.expected_output: Identical task to pf-critical-1 but with NO /plan prefix. The wording ('How should I approach', 'Walk me through the plan before we implement') strongly sounds like planning and could fool the model into thinking it is in plan mode — but no /plan was entered, so plan mode is NOT active. Per SKILL.md the skill must stay silent: NO '## Preflight:' header and NO 'Execution fit:' verdict. The model may discuss the approach in prose, just without invoking preflight.

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain a '## Preflight:' header
assertions.description: Plan-sounding wording without a /plan prefix must NOT invoke preflight — this is the core false-positive guard

assertions.text: Response does NOT contain an 'Execution fit:' verdict line
assertions.description: No preflight report should be emitted when the user is not actually in plan mode

evals.prompt:
I'm planning to call crc16_update() from my 1 ms control ISR. Work out whether it fits. Session context: LOCI target: armv6-m; this repository has no `.loci/contract.yaml`. The CFG `loci elf asm` printed for crc16_update carries:
loops: 2 (1 with a derived trip count; max nesting depth 1)
  iters = executions of a block per single call of crc16_update (product of enclosing trip counts);
  ? = not derivable from the code — treat that block's cost as per-iteration, not per-call.
  A block with no iters annotation is in no loop and runs once per call.
  L1  loop  header bb_0x24  latch bb_0x2e  depth 1  blocks 2  source=crc16.c:18:5  trips 8 exact  (init r4=0 @bb_0x20; step +1 (adds r4, #1 @bb_0x2e); limit 8 (cmp r4, #8 @bb_0x2e); continue on lt)
  L2  loop  header bb_0x40  latch bb_0x52  depth 1  blocks 3  source=crc16.c:31:5  trips ?  reason=init-not-visible (no constant initialiser for r2 reaching bb_0x3c)
and its blocks carry iters=8 inside the first loop and iters=? inside the second. Hot-path block costs sum to 300 ns if every block is counted once. (Grade only the reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)
evals.expected_output: Does NOT report 300 ns as the worst path or as the call's cost: that sum counts every block once. Computes no cost of its own for the call — no block-times-iters product, total or cost formula — and does not offer to do that arithmetic itself later; stating the given sum as a floor (`≥ 300 ns`, the real cost is above it) is the lower-bound treatment the skill prescribes and is fine, because the skill's Step 3 says path cost, in every part, is `loci analyse measure`'s arithmetic and a hand-derived figure is a different measurement. It leaves the figure to a LOCI measurement (`loci analyse measure`, `/loci:exec-trace` or a preflight re-run — any of them counts) and says it is a `≥` lower bound while the second loop's trip count is not derivable. A qualitative remark is fine: that the given 300 ns sum is a small share of 1 ms but only a floor, or that the first loop's 8 iterations raise the cost by a fixed factor. Names the uncountable loop by where it is in the source (crc16.c:31) and gives its reason (no constant initialiser for r2) and its trip count as not derivable; a mention of the first loop carries its 8 iterations (exact). The `L2` id never stands in for the source location; echoing it beside the location, as the user's own message spells it, is tolerated. Assigns no number to the second loop's trip count and does not treat iters=? as 1; saying what probably drives it (a length argument, the caller's buffer) without putting a number on it is fine. Does not present the fit with the 1 ms ISR as settled: an ADJUST PLAN, a GOOD that says no contract covers the signal and names the second loop as undecided, or no opinion all count. It has that loop's bound come from somewhere other than an assumption, and any one route counts: the user stating the maximum, a cap or termination guard at the call site or in the function, or a bound declared in the repository's Contract Envelope.

assertions.text: Does not report 300 ns as the worst path or as the call's cost
assertions.description: the bare-sum figure is the failure this guards

assertions.text: Computes no cost of its own for the call (no block-times-iters product, total or cost formula) and does not offer to compute it by hand; leaves the figure to a LOCI measurement (`loci analyse measure`, `/loci:exec-trace` or a preflight re-run all count) and says it is a `≥` lower bound while the second loop's count is not derivable (stating `≥ 300 ns` as a floor is fine)
assertions.description: SKILL.md Step 3: 'Do not compute any of this yourself. Path cost, in every part, is measure's arithmetic.' The old rubric demanded the multiplication the skill forbids (AAD-8002)

assertions.text: Names the uncountable loop by its source location (crc16.c:31), with its reason and its trip count as not derivable; the `L2` id never stands in for the location
assertions.description: house rules, Naming a path or a loop: by source range when the row has one; the trip count always goes with it. An id echoed beside the location is tolerated because the user's message spells the loops that way

assertions.text: Assigns no number to the second loop's trip count and does not treat iters=? as 1 (naming what probably drives it, without a number, is fine)
assertions.description: a guessed bound is a fabricated number

assertions.text: Does not present the fit with the 1 ms ISR as settled (ADJUST PLAN, a GOOD naming the second loop as undecided, or no opinion all count), and has that loop's bound come from the user, a cap or termination guard, or the Contract Envelope rather than an assumption; any one route counts
assertions.description: SKILL.md: a lower bound 'can only grow' and its reason goes in the Note; with no contract the word is the agent's and a GOOD must say no contract covers the signal; 'An unbounded loop in a callee -> plan to add a termination guard or budget'. No-GOOD is not demanded: the rule against a check mark on a `>=` lives in compile-route.md, which run_evals.sh does not inline

evals.prompt: Decision question, no tools needed — reason it out from the loci-preflight skill and answer directly. The session context carries `loci: CLI is 0.2.2 but this plugin pins 0.2.120 — the automatic upgrade is not taking effect. A retry runs in the background this session; if the user hits stale behaviour or asks about the version, invoke the loci:setup skill and read `…/loci-cli-install.log` for the cause.` In /plan mode I asked you to add a callee to an existing function, so preflight is running. The project does have a `.loci/build.yaml`. Step 1's `loci analyse prepare --source … --functions … --signals hot_path_time,worst_path_time,energy --phase preflight --turn … --caller loci-preflight` produced no JSON at all — stdout was empty and stderr read exactly `usage: loci [-h] [-V] <command> ...` then `loci: error: unrecognized arguments: --signals hot_path_time,worst_path_time,energy`, with exit code 2. What do you do next, and what does the preflight report say?
evals.expected_output: Recognises exit 2 with an argparse usage message, empty stdout and no JSON as the installed CLI being older than the plugin's pin (the stale-CLI advisory says so) — NOT as the user's code failing to compile, and not as one of the coded errors: there is no envelope, so there is no `.ok` and no `error.code` to branch on. Does not write around it: does not re-run `prepare` without `--signals` (or with any other flag dropped or changed), does not fall back to `loci build compile`, a hand compile, or a project-built .o or .elf, and does not proceed to `loci analyse measure`. Reports no timing or energy figure, since nothing was measured, and says the CLI is too old as an action, not as a version number — run `/loci:setup` to repair the install — then stops; a '## Preflight: STOPPED' block carrying that sentence is a fine way to say it. Prints no `Recipe:` provenance line (preflight prints one in no case). (Grade only this reasoning; the agent need not execute any loci command.)

assertions.text: Recognises exit 2 with an argparse usage message and empty stdout as the installed CLI being older than the plugin's pin, not as the user's code failing to compile and not as a coded `error.code` refusal
assertions.description: house rules: argparse exits 2 with no JSON at all, where `.ok` is neither true nor false; the stale-CLI advisory names the skew

assertions.text: Does not re-run `prepare` with `--signals` (or any other flag) dropped, and does not fall back to `loci build compile`, a hand compile, or a project-built .o or .elf
assertions.description: the old cascade's re-run-without-the-flag recovery is gone; writing around a too-old CLI is the failure this guards

assertions.text: Does not proceed to `loci analyse measure` and reports no timing or energy figure
assertions.description: nothing was prepared, so there is nothing to measure

assertions.text: Offers `/loci:setup` as the fix, saying the CLI is too old as an action rather than quoting its version number, and stops
assertions.description: house rules, Reporting versions: a CLI that is too old is said as an action (run /loci:setup)

assertions.text: Prints no `Recipe:` provenance line
assertions.description: SKILL.md 'One exception, one line': preflight prints none in any case (lib/eval-graders.sh names this eval as its pin)
